moat_against: ROIC proxy 1.2% (2023), 2.0% (2024), 5.2% (2025) — below cost of capital through the available history; gross margin compressed 17.5% -> 11.8% (2022-2025) as mix shifted to pass-through pharmacy revenue
Reimbursement is set by Medicare/Medicaid/commercial payers, not the company — IRA impact ~$200M on Home & Community Pharmacy in 2026, that segment's revenue fell 8.6% in H1 2026
Insurer-owned rivals (UnitedHealth/Optum, CVS) and focused peers (Option Care) compete for the same specialty/infusion volume
Labor-intensive provider services with thin operating margins (0.8-2.3% FY2023-25) and clinician-retention risk on acquired Amedisys/LHC branches
Levered history and sponsor overhang: KKR secondary offering in June 2026; net debt $2.42B at FY2025
moat_for: National scale in home/community care for complex populations — ~475,000 patients daily, national payer contracts and procurement leverage
Limited-distribution drug portfolio (149 drugs, 16-20 launches expected next 12-18 months) — access smaller specialty pharmacies cannot replicate
Integrated Pharmacy Solutions + Provider Services platform: cross-referrals, sticky clinically-managed infusion/specialty cases with complex payer authorization
Specialty & Infusion momentum: Q2 2026 revenue +30%, script growth +31%
moat_justification: Scale, limited-distribution drug access (149 drugs) and an integrated pharmacy+provider platform give sticky clinical/payer relationships, but ROIC proxy was only 1.2%/2.0%/5.2% in 2023/2024/2025 and gross margin fell from 17.5% (2022) to 11.8% (2025) on low-margin specialty pharmacy mix — no proven pricing power or through-cycle returns above the cost of capital.
name: BrightSpring Health Services, Inc.
one_liner: Real growth pharmacy/provider platform, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% at $60.87 on any scenario (weighted IRR 7.2%, weighted IV@15% $21.05; clears 15% only below ~$21) despite +23% Q2 revenue growth, because TTM OE is only $1.57/share and margins/ROIC are thin.
